_note: Pages permitted to read a person's `living` flag directly, each with the
reason. Everything that decides whether to PUBLISH A NAME goes through
publishableOrNamed() — because on 22 September a page wrote that rule out
for itself and published forty-four living people.
COUNTING IS NOT PUBLISHING, and a gate that cannot tell them apart forces a
page that only wants a number through a publishing helper, which teaches the
next author that the helpers are ceremony. So the legitimate direct reads are
declared here rather than forbidden, and an UNDECLARED one refuses the build.
A page in this list is not exempt from the rule. It is exempt from the
HELPER, having stated why it does not need it.

16 October 2026: the rule changed from «no living person is a page» to «a living person is a name, a relationship, a town and a country». The helpers keep their names and now mean «may be named»; the gate still refuses a page that decides for itself who is drawn or what a living row carries.

allow.why: A CONFIDENCE LABEL, not a name. The chart draws the word «living» in place of a generation it will not name, which is the rule being obeyed rather than bypassed — the page never had the name to publish.

PASSES THE FLAG ONWARD to the kit's Descent row, which suppresses dates, places, notes and children itself. Replacing this with a helper would strip the flag and leave the component unable to do its own suppression — the one case where reading `living` directly is what keeps somebody hidden.

allow.use: const alive = !!p.living  (chooses which fields of a row to draw)
allow.why: A ROW'S FIELDS, not a filter. Until 16 October 2026 this page hand-rolled f.members.filter((m) => !m.living) and published forty-four living people on the day it was written; under the standard of that date (a living person is a name, a relationship, a town and a country) the row is drawn for every member and `alive` only decides which fields it carries: no era, no born, no died, no trade, no marriage date, no confidence. Declared rather than refused because the choice IS the rule, and the data holds nothing else for it to leak.
